extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors submitting manuscripts to Science (AAAS/Science magazine)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for preparing and submitting manuscripts (Research Articles, Reports, Brevia, Comments, and commentary) to Science magazine, including formatting, data/deposition, embargo, and editorial policies. Geared to researchers/authors seeking publication in Science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and broad importance
rubrics_metrics.description: For original research, the common thread is that the work should reveal novel concepts of broad importance to the scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science is interested in a wide range of manuscripts presenting original research and commentary in all areas of science; submissions should report primary data and the main conclusions for the first time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript categories and length limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories include Research Articles (up to ~4,500 words), Reports (up to 2,500 words), Brevia (~800 words), and Technical Comments (~750 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical Comments are brief, comment on previously published research, are published online with an abstract in print, and are indexed on Medline. Commentary forms (Editorials, Perspectives, Reviews, etc.) are usually solicited but occasionally considered unsolicited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance rate / competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Science can accept less than 10% of original research papers submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most submissions are evaluated by staff editors and the Board of Reviewing Editors for significance, quality, and interest. About 75% of submitted manuscripts are rejected during initial screening, usually within one week to 10 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Science treats all submitted manuscripts as confidential documents and expects reviewers and Board members to do likewise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review process is confidential and identities of reviewers are not released. Letters and Technical Comments sent to authors for response are otherwise treated the same with respect to confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science Express rapid-publication policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected topical papers are posted online by Science Express two to six weeks ahead of print publication and are considered published on the posting date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science Express usually selects several papers per week; online posting date is the publication date and print versions indicate the online publication date. Access policies (AAAS members free, nominal fee for nonmembers) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of non-U.S. authors / global submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Science welcomes submissions from non-U.S. authors and is interested in publishing the best papers from all countries and regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic submission is preferred to minimize mail delays. The Board and referees include substantial international representation; the journal maintains a European office and pursues access arrangements in developing regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo policy rules
rubrics_metrics.description: No news coverage of a paper may appear before 2:00 p.m. Eastern U.S. Time on the Thursday before the paper's publication (Science publishes each Friday, except last Friday of the year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientists may present results at professional meetings to colleagues; if accepted, inform AAAS News and Information. Comments to reporters at meetings should be limited to clarifying the presentation; do not expand beyond the talk or give copies of the paper/data to reporters. Do not give interviews on the work until the week before publication (only if the journalist agrees to abide by the embargo). Do not participate in news conferences until after 1:00 p.m. Eastern the day before publication. Contact AAAS News and Information Office for questions; full policy mailed upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright and exclusive publication license
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors retain copyright of their work but must grant an exclusive publication license to Science and AAAS for acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further license details available from the journal; authors with questions should contact a deputy editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously published work, in English or another language, cannot be submitted as a Report, Research Article, or Brevia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science will only consider research papers reporting primary data and main conclusions for the first time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on manuscripts posted online before submission (preprints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Posting of manuscript copies on the Internet may be considered prior publication that could compromise originality of the Science submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting copies at not-for-profit publicly funded web archives is allowed immediately upon publication. For postings on preprint servers, authors should contact the editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and materials availability / deposition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: As a condition of publication, authors must agree to honor reasonable requests for materials and methods necessary to verify conclusions and make the data available to the scientific community in some form for verification and replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large datasets (DNA/protein sequences, microarray data, crystal structures) generally must be deposited before publication in approved public databases (e.g., GenBank, SwissPROT, PDB) with accession numbers provided; coordinates must be released at time of publication. Other supporting data can be posted on Science Online as supporting online material.

rubrics_metrics.name: PubMed Central (PMC) deposit policy for NIH-funded papers
rubrics_metrics.description: For a paper created under an NIH grant and accepted on or after 2 May 2005, authors may post the 'accepted version' to PMC no sooner than six months after final publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'accepted version' is the version after peer-review changes but before Science's editing/production. Authors of NIH-funded Science papers should set the public release time at six months after final publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation differences for initial submission vs. resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines differ for initial submission and for resubmission after peer review; follow the specific instructions for each stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For initial submissions, follow instructions in the left-hand column of the manuscript-preparation page; for resubmissions use the right-hand column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure submission differences (initial vs. revised)
rubrics_metrics.description: For new manuscript submissions, figures should generally be included as part of a single manuscript file; for resubmissions, figures should be submitted separately from text and tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If high-resolution prints are required for proper evaluation (e.g., micrographs), send them separately by mail and note separate submission in the cover letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimum resolution for figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution depends on stage: for initial submissions (peer review) embed figures at 150–300 dpi to keep file sizes reasonable; for revised manuscripts submit separate files at higher resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For revised manuscripts, minimum 400 dpi for grayscale and color artwork and 1200 dpi for digital line art (refers to images sized comparable to print figures). Reducing/enlarging raster images changes resolution. See detailed instructions for revised manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting online material standards and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting online material consists of additional material (text, tables, diagrams, images, video, sound files) that bear directly on conclusions but cannot be accommodated in print; it must be essential to the scientific integrity and excellence of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporting online material is subject to the same editorial standards and peer-review as the print publication. For new manuscript submissions, include most supplemental data in the main manuscript file; for revised manuscripts upload supplemental data as separate individual files. Read detailed guidelines on preparing supporting online material.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to refer to supporting online material
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriate style for referencing supporting online material is specified in the journal's supporting-online-material guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consult the specific guidelines page for proper citation/style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover image submission criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit an image for consideration as the cover; the cover is usually related to a particularly significant Report or Research Article or special issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images that are striking to the nonspecialist and related to significant papers have the best chance. Images not used on the cover may be used on the table of contents or in 'This Week in Science'. For resubmissions the upload form includes a field for cover candidates; hard copy images may be sent directly to the handling editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should assemble electronic files and proceed to initial submission or revised manuscript upload site; online submission is strongly recommended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Online submission is optimized for editorial/workflow and speeds consideration. Expect an e-mail acknowledgment within one to two full business days after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directing manuscripts to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not required to address a paper to a specific editor when submitting a new manuscript, but you may direct the cover letter to the editor who handles the subject area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list of editors and subject areas is available on the staff page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on mailing hard-copy materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not mail a hard copy in addition to submitting online (it may delay processing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions for initial submission: you may need to send figures, reference material, or supporting online material separately by mail if inclusion would exceed the 6 MB upload limit. If sending images separately, mention this in the cover letter. Supporting online material should generally be included at the end of the main manuscript file unless size limits require separate mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission after rejection / appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally not advisable to revise and resubmit a rejected manuscript; most editorial decisions are based on technical merit, general interest, importance, and comparison with other papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science will only reconsider papers when specifically invited to resubmit or when a significant error in review determined the decision. Editors will entertain appeals (best by email), but most papers are not reconsidered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer turnaround and publication timeline expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to return comments within two weeks; some papers can be reviewed within 48 hours for rapid assessment. Most papers are published within 14 weeks of initial submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Science Express can publish certain papers within ten days to two weeks of acceptance, and sometimes within two weeks of receipt. Initial electronic evaluation by the Board of Reviewing Editors typically has a 48-hour turnaround for screening.
